name: Pediatric posterior approach to the humeral shaft
corridor: Posterior midline approach, triceps-sparing or triceps-splitting, protecting the radial nerve in the spiral groove and the ulnar nerve, to expose the distal humerus in a child

positioning.text: Position prone or lateral with the arm over a bolster and the elbow flexed so the posterior arm is presented.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the tip of the olecranon and the posterior midline of the arm.

incision.text: Run a straight posterior midline incision proximally from the olecranon, aware that it crosses the radial and axillary nerve territories at different levels.

superficial_interval.text: Prefer a triceps-sparing elevation that leaves the triceps insertion undisturbed, or use a triceps split, which carries a higher risk of radial nerve injury.

deep_interval.text: Identify and protect the radial nerve and profunda brachii in the spiral groove, using an age-based safe zone (in younger children the window between the distal physis and about 1 cm per year of age proximal to it), and loop the ulnar nerve medially.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, deep fascia, the triceps, the radial and ulnar nerves, and the posterior humerus.

structures_at_risk.text: The radial nerve with the profunda brachii in the spiral groove and the ulnar nerve medially are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The spiral groove is the danger zone for the radial nerve, and a triceps split increases that risk; the safe bony window is age-dependent.

retraction_hazards.text: Loop and protect the ulnar nerve and avoid uncontrolled traction on the triceps and both nerves.

exposure.text: Exposes the distal posterior humerus in a child for fracture fixation.

limitations.text: The radial nerve safe zone is age-dependent and limits proximal extension, and a triceps split trades wider access for greater nerve risk.

indications.text: Indicated for open reduction and fixation of pediatric distal humeral shaft fractures approached posteriorly.

closure.text: Reattach or lay back the triceps and close the wound in layers with resorbable sutures.

complications.text: Complications include radial nerve palsy, ulnar nerve irritation, and triceps weakness.

procedure_applications.condition: A pediatric distal humeral shaft fracture is plated posteriorly

questions.question: Which posterior technique is preferred in children and why?
questions.answer: Triceps-sparing, because it preserves triceps integrity and lowers radial nerve risk compared with a split.

questions.question: How is the radial nerve safe zone estimated in a young child?
questions.answer: The window between the distal physis and about 1 cm per year of age proximal to it.

questions.question: Which nerve is looped and protected medially?
